(Houston, Texas) | college = [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] (2014–2017) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2017 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2017]]) * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2017 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2017]]) *[[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]] (2017) *First-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] (2017) *ACC All-Freshman team (2015) *[[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014]]) *[[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] co-MVP ([[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014]]) *[[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2014) | medal_templates = {{MedalCountry|the {{USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|FIBA Americas U16 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|2011 Mexico]] | [[United States men's national basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Justin Aaron Jackson''' (born March 28, 1995) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played basketball in the Homeschool Christian Youth Association (HCYA), Jackson committed to play with the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball]] team after being rated as the 8th best player of his class by [[ESPN|ESPN Recruiting Nation]]. The [[small forward]] took part in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], and was named Co-MVP along with [[Jahlil Okafor]]. == High school career == [[File:20140402 MCDAAG MVPs (2).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Jackson and [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] co-MVP [[Jahlil Okafor]]]] Jackson played [[basketball]] for Homeschool Christian Youth Association (HCYA), a nonprofit Christian service organization created to serve home school families and students in [[Houston]] and the surrounding area.{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=The life of Justin Jackson|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2013/the-life-of-justin-jackson|accessdate=April 19, 2017|work=[[USA Today]]|date=December 10, 2013}} He led the Warriors to a national championship in the 2012 season, a massive factor in winning the Sullivan Award. He continued to shine in his final year, averaging 31.5 points and 9.1 rebounds in his successful last season.{{cite web|title=Justin Jackson Bio|url=http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=3350&ATCLID=209532765|website=GoHeels.com|accessdate=16 July 2014}} Jackson became known as one of the most potent [[high school]] athletes in the nation which promptly triggered a highly publicized recruitment. He was given offers by [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]], [[Georgetown University men's basketball|Georgetown]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|North Carolina State]], [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], and [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]]. Jackson was rated a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], [[ESPN]], and [[247Sports.com]]. Eventually, the [[small forward]] signed with North Carolina. He was marked as one of the top players in the Class of 2014.{{cite web|title=Justin Jackson|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Justin-Jackson-113617|website=Yahoo.com|accessdate=16 July 2014}}{{cite web|title=Justin Jackson|url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/102457/justin-jackson|website=ESPN.com|accessdate=16 July 2014}}{{cite web|title=Justin Jackson|url=http://247sports.com/Player/Justin-Jackson-14192|website=247Sports.com|accessdate=16 July 2014}} Following his years with HCYA, Jackson was named to the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] on January 29, 2014. After scoring the first few points of the game, the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] recruit was named co-MVP with [[Jahlil Okafor]]. Jackson ended with 23 points off 11-of-12 shooting, making him the game's top scorer. He also won the Jack Daly Award for sportsmanship.{{cite web|last1=Johnson|first1=Chris|title=2014 McDonald's All-American game: Okafor, Jackson take home MVP honors|url=http://www.si.com/college-basketball/one-and-one/2014/04/03/mcdonalds-all-american-game-jahlil-okafor-justin-jackson|website=SI.com|accessdate=16 July 2014}} == College career == In his three year college career, Justin Jackson won ACC Player of the Year, was selected as First-team All ACC, and was named a Consensus first-team All-American in 2017. Jackson scored sixteen points and picked up four rebounds in the Tar Heels 6th championship title in the [[2017 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]]. On April 13, 2017, Jackson declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last1=Goodman|first1=Jeff|title=Justin Jackson leaves UNC after junior season to enter NBA draft|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19149303/justin-jackson-leaves-north-carolina-tar-heels-enter-nba-draft|website=ESPN|publisher=ESPN Insider|accessdate=13 April 2017}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == {{Commons category|Justin Jackson}} *[http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=3350&ATCLID=209532765 GoHeels.com Bio] *[http://archive.usab.com/bios/jackson_justin.html USA Basketball bio] {{navboxes|list= {{2017 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{2017 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball navbox}} {{Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{McDonald's All-American Game Boys MVP}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Jackson, Justin}} [[Category:1995 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2016 NCAA Men's Division I Final Four]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2017 NCAA Men's Division I Final Four]] [[Category:Basketball players from Texas]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball players]] [[Category:Parade High School All-Americans (boys' basketball)]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Houston]]
